brief: Goldman's TMT desk note frames Friday's tape around the September payrolls print: GS forecasts +80k, below the +88k consensus, as futures rally and yields ease off highs. Oil falls on talk that European governments, including France, may release diesel and crude reserves. Premarket moves cluster around single-name news: STX and WDC fall on reports Toshiba will double HDD production capacity by fiscal 2027 to fill an AI-driven storage gap, ON rises after sweetening its Synaptics acquisition to an all-cash $5.7bn/$123-per-share deal from a stock offer near $7bn, APP extends a 13-of-14-session slide on a bearish note, and TWLO rises on its S&P 500 addition. Separately, Amazon is reported seeking to offload $8bn of Nvidia chips into a leased-back special-purpose vehicle funded by debt, an asset-light balance-sheet move. In research, GS maintains its Sell on Adobe despite a new CEO it frames as a possible AI-turnaround catalyst, wanting proof of execution first. A Micron read-across argues 2027-2028 memory supply/demand tightens versus 2026, supporting reiterated Buy ratings on Samsung and SK Hynix as Korean DRAM exports hit a record $33bn, up 552% year over year.
